Initial unsubmitted source-audited draft.

section1.p: Unsubmitted ProtoXEP draft, version 0.0.1. This document has not been accepted, assigned a number or approved by the XMPP Standards Foundation. It records the compatibility behavior in Monogram 0.2.195 at commit 4736f7eddb423192e5d68435879f0b0a88371168.

Normative words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY describe conformance to this document, not XSF approval. Existing deployed identifiers are retained; no urn:xmpp namespace is invented or reserved by this draft.

An account can suggest an image without being authorized to modify the recipient profile. Existing file-sharing and avatar publication protocols do the transport and eventual publication. The only deployed suggestion signal is an ordinary image caption; there is no private avatar-suggestion stanza or automatic profile write.

The sender transmits an ordinary image through the selected file-sharing/encryption transport with the exact caption Suggested profile photo. The recipient may offer a separate explicit action to choose/crop/adopt that image. Adopting publishes the recipient own avatar through the normal authorized avatar flow. Otherwise the message remains an ordinary image/caption. The phrase is wire compatibility text; local action labels can be translated.

example.caption: Caption convention; FILE SHARING represents the normal existing attachment payload

section1.example: <message xmlns='jabber:client' to='juliet@example.org' type='chat'> <body>Suggested profile photo https://files.example.org/suggestion.png</body> <!-- Normal XEP-0447 attachment metadata accompanies this body. --> </message>
section1.p: There is no suggestion-specific acknowledgment, ownership transfer, remote approval result, overwrite command or automatic acceptance. The caption is not authenticated more strongly than the containing message. Native rendering is optional; unsupported clients still show the image and caption.

No suggestion-specific feature is advertised. A sender cannot assume the recipient offers an adoption action. Invalid/unsupported media retains normal attachment error behavior. Before adoption validate the downloaded image, offer the normal review/crop controls and retain the current avatar on cancellation or failure. The receiver must not silently download/publish it because a caption matches.

Clients MUST retain a readable textual representation, expose actions and state to assistive technology, and avoid making color, animation or an icon the sole indicator of meaning. Unsupported metadata MUST NOT hide the readable fallback.

Message text is Unicode. Fixed protocol tokens are case-sensitive and MUST NOT be translated; human-facing labels MAY be localized. Implementations MUST distinguish UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar/code-point offsets and UTF-16 code-unit limits wherever this document specifies them. They MUST reject invalid encoding rather than replacing bytes in an identifier or payment destination.

Any correspondent can type this caption. It MUST NOT grant profile-write authority or bypass image validation and explicit user consent. Only the recipient authenticated account may publish the adopted avatar.

The sender-chosen image may contain private metadata or identify a third party. Publishing an avatar changes its audience independently of the private suggestion message; the adoption UI must make that publication intentional.
This document requests no IANA action. No media type or URI scheme is registered by publication of this draft.
This draft requests no new registration. Existing protocol namespaces retain their existing ownership and meaning.

The following source files and implementation notes are pinned to the audited commit. Existing regression tests are implementation evidence, not an independent interoperability or security audit. Editorial review can change a future proposal, but changes to deployed wire syntax require an explicit version/migration path.
